## Body

# Security verdict, #330 round 1 at 1c998e75d005eaa70266314da25a533204ab7f70: pass

Static review of crates/tmux/src/lib.rs (detach_pane_taps), pane_observer.rs, lib.rs (shutdown), death_sweep.rs and the fakes, in a detached worktree. CI SUCCESS at this head.

## The batched tmux command line
No shell, and no injection.
- `run()` executes tmux through `Command::args(args)` (lib.rs:430-436), with no `sh -c`. Each pane id is its own argv element after `-t`.
- tmux treats only an argv element that is exactly `;` as a command separator, and `-t` targets are not format-expanded. A pane id therefore cannot open a new tmux command or reach a shell.
- The ids come from `tracked_panes()`, which are the observer's own tmux-listed `%N` ids.
- No sink path appears on the command line: `pipe-pane -t <pane>` with no command only closes the pipe, and `set-option -p -u -t <pane> <TAP_SINK_OPTION>` unsets a constant option name.
- Length: about 11 argv elements per pane, so a few thousand short strings at 200+ panes, far under ARG_MAX.

## Foreign taps are never touched
Ownership is decided per pane before the batch is built:
- a tap this daemon tracks locally (`self.taps`), or
- a listed tap whose marker equals `expected_tap_sink(pane)`.

A pane with no marker is refused ("no owned tap"), and a marker that doesn't match is refused ("refusing to detach foreign tap"). Neither goes into `pending`, so neither is in the launched argv. Later rounds rebuild the argv only from `pending`, which retain() narrows. The real-tmux test pins a foreign tap being left alone.

## render::seat (my #325 note)
Closed. death_sweep.rs's alarm body now names each seat through `pij_core::render::seat`, and `the_alarm_names_seats_only_through_their_grammar` pins it, with mutant D3 RED.

## Other
AbortOnDrop and the release-after-detach ordering are correctness and liveness changes for the reviewer. They decide no authority. They launch nothing new beyond the single batched launch, which is one launch per stop, replacing two per pane. D-F267-4 (a late `cat >>` recreating an empty sink) is in the observer's own sink directory and pre-existing; it is not cross-seat. No secrets, lockfile or `.npmrc` changes.
